text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday:

- Jewish organisations were incensed when Swiss President Jean-Pascal Delamuraz called the $250 million fund demanded of Switzerland for Jewish Holocaust victims "ransom money". Delamuraz later said his remark was misunderstood.
- Annual inflation, at 0.8 percent in 1996, was at the lowest level in Switzerland in 10 years.
- The percentage of foreigners living in Zurich at the end of 1995 -- 28.9 percent -- was practically identical to the figure in 1900.
- Switzerland's year as head of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe came to an end; Denmark has now taken over.
- Consumer credits in Switzerland have fallen by 29.1 percent to 5.5 billion Swiss francs since the recession began in 1991.
- The number of daily newspapers in Switzerland fell to 99 in 1996. In 1980 there were 126 dailies throughout the country.
- Nearly 6,200 or 1.3 percent fewer passengers used Geneva's Cointrin airport in 1996 compared to the year before.
